title: Primitive induction, conductor, and bad-prime correction
pvg_object: residue-coordinate phase data with modulus labels and exceptional prime coordinates dividing the modulus
ant_object: an imprimitive Dirichlet character, its primitive inducing character, conductor, and finite Euler correction product
forward_translation: Replace an imprimitive L-function by the primitive inducing L-function only together with the exact finite Euler factors at primes dividing the modulus but not the conductor.
reverse_translation: The primitive character plus modulus and correction factors reconstructs the imprimitive twist; the primitive L-function alone loses bad-prime local data.
preserved_information: primitive global phase, conductor, and explicitly retained bad-prime factors
lost_information: omitted correction factors change constants and may alter local zeros or cancellations
trigger: A character modulo q is induced from a smaller conductor or a proof changes modulus conventions.
typical_output: a normalized primitive factorization with exact local corrections
error_or_wall: Silent primitive replacement can corrupt residues, leading constants, and uniform conductor dependence.
required_certificate: Identify the conductor and inducing character, state the finite correction product prime by prime, and track it through residues and bounds.
positive_example: L(s,chi_0 mod 4)=zeta(s)(1-2^{-s}); the missing factor is not optional.
counterexample: Replacing L(s,chi_0 mod 4) by zeta(s) changes the residue at s=1.
anti_overclaim: Primitive reduction is a normalization step, not equality without correction factors.
source_basis: Classical theory of primitive and imprimitive Dirichlet characters

title: From moments to exceptional sets and maximal control
pvg_object: energy of residue fibers or coordinate observables after aggregation
ant_object: L2 or higher-moment estimates, tail probabilities, exceptional sets, and L-infinity bounds
forward_translation: Convert a moment bound only through Markov, Chebyshev, large-deviation, maximal, or amplification inequalities, recording the resulting exceptional-set size and loss.
reverse_translation: Pointwise control implies moment control, but a moment alone recovers only a distributional envelope, not each fiber.
preserved_information: average energy and the tail bounds explicitly derived from it
lost_information: phase, location of exceptional classes, and sharp maximum size
trigger: A mean-square theorem is used to claim a bound for every residue class or every parameter.
typical_output: a quantified exceptional set or a named L2-to-Linfinity obstruction
error_or_wall: Rare spikes may saturate the moment while violating a uniform bound.
required_certificate: State the moment order, normalization, threshold, exceptional-set estimate, and any maximal or amplification input.
positive_example: An L2 bound gives a Chebyshev exceptional-set bound, not a pointwise theorem for all classes.
counterexample: Vectors with the same L2 norm can have very different maxima.
anti_overclaim: Never replace average control by uniform control without a maximal certificate.
